definition: The instruction-tuned 7B Qwen2.5 vision-language model, used across 3 sources as the standard multimodal evaluation subject. Its most informative archived appearance is in a consistency-based selection audit finding that a published result is driven by the decoding format rather than by the perturbation it was attributed to -- one of the archive's clearest instances of an effect belonging to the apparatus. It also appears as the backbone for perception-versus-reasoning latent routing and for confidence-aware medical training.

evidence.note: Shows that a perturbation-based selection rule's apparent 31.8-point gain over majority voting in vision-language test-time scaling is a decoding-format effect, by adding a control that spends the same short-answer budget on the unperturbed image and finds it matches or beats the perturbation rule everywhere.
evidence.title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Splits a video model's latent computation into perception latents that always ground the question in visual evidence and reasoning latents allocated only when the question needs inference, and shows that reasoning latents without rationale supervision are worse than no reasoning latents at all.
evidence.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

evidence.note: Adds a correctness-conditioned confidence term to the GRPO reward for medical visual question answering -- rewarding answer-token confidence when the answer is right and penalising it when wrong -- on top of an SFT cold start built from answer-conditioned reasoning traces filtered by a verifier.
evidence.title: CARE: Confidence-Aware Reasoning for Reliable Medical VQA

name: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
